current_activity: Walcheren: 157th Brigade relieves the Canadians at the causeway and wades the Sloe Channel at 03:30 on 3 Nov
notes: Event date: 3 November 1944, 03:30 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 111, 114). Event definition: After the Canadian attacks of 31 October and 1-2 November, a battalion of the 157th Brigade relieves the Canadians at the Walcheren causeway on 2 November under cover of Typhoon rockets; at 03:30 on the 3rd the brigade outflanks the causeway by crossing the Sloe Channel in boats and wading a mile along the mud shore, without serious opposition; the 156th Brigade follows on the 4th and both brigades then link up and advance towards Middelburg (p. 114); the earlier landing on South Beveland, with the leading troops of the division crossing the Scheldt, is dated about 26 October (p. 111). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 114: "Then under cover of a heavy rocket attack by Typhoons they were relieved by a battalion of the 157th Brigade of the 52nd (Lowland) Division"; "At 3.30 on the morning of the 3rd this was done without serious opposition"; p. 111: "the 52nd Division's leading troops had crossed the Scheldt and were landing on South Beveland". Location: Sloedam (Walcheren causeway), Zeeland (existing place PL0685) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the Sloedam causeway, where the brigade crossed the channel; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the Walcheren causeway and the Sloe Channel crossing (p. 114).
